topics: t084 Normalisation of deviance and drift
key: Normalization of deviance (Vaughan): accepting events that aren't supposed to happen until the deviation is viewed as normal and acceptable; NASA kept flying with foam losses on that basis.
key_elements: accepting a deviation that isn't supposed to happen until it is seen as normal or acceptable
past occurrences without disaster taken as evidence it is safe, or the foam-loss history named

topics: t056 Manoeuvre warfare and the nature of war
key: Friction: the countless factors that make the apparently easy so difficult (Clausewitz); it resists all action, saps energy, and makes the simple difficult.
key_elements: the concept named friction
the many small factors that make what should be easy or simple hard

key: Avoid counterfactual arguments ('if this person had done X, the accident would not have occurred'); learn why people did what they did, why it made sense to them at the time.
key_elements: advises against the if-only / should-have framing (counterfactuals)
instead learn why the action made sense to the person at the time

key: The Definition of Done: a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the product's quality measures; it gives everyone a shared understanding, and an item that doesn't meet it can't be released or presented at the Sprint Review.
key_elements: a shared, formal definition of the quality state work must reach (Definition of Done)
work that doesn't meet it isn't released or presented (returns to the backlog)

section.name: Vertical Dimension of Org Design: Work Mandate

key: Scope of work mandate: the vertical axis of the Org Topologies map, the scope of work given to a unit, from tasks at the bottom up to overlapping, co-owned scopes (team-of-teams) at the top; the higher, the bigger its field of play.
key_elements: named as work mandate (scope of work), the vertical axis of the Org Topologies map
levels from narrow tasks upward, a higher level meaning a bigger field of play

topics: t004 Human error and human performance
t078 Controls and defence in depth
key: The paper plant: the aggregate of all the documentation that controls the configuration of the physical plant; flaws in it can lie dormant and lead to bad outcomes or injury in the physical plant.
key_elements: named as the paper plant (the documentation that controls the physical plant)
flaws in it lie dormant and later cause harm in the physical plant

topics: t034 Mental health and psychological disorders

section.name: 15.3 The Diathesis-Stress Model of Psychological Disorders

key: The diathesis-stress model: people with an underlying predisposition (diathesis) are more likely to develop a disorder when faced with adverse events (stress); both are necessary, and the more predisposition, the less stress is needed.
key_elements: an underlying predisposition (diathesis) plus adverse events (stress)
both needed, or the stress needed falls as the predisposition rises

key: Equity theory: motivation depends on our outcomes for our inputs compared with others' outcomes and inputs; perceived unfairness (underreward) lowers satisfaction and effort.
key_elements: named as equity theory
comparing one's own outcome-to-input ratio with a coworker's, with perceived unfairness lowering motivation

section.name: Brief 1.07 System Archetypes, Archetype #1: Fixes that fail

key: The 'fixes that fail' archetype: a short-term fix solves the problem in the short run but generates unintended consequences that make the original problem worse.
key_elements: named as fixes that fail (a system archetype)
short-term fix whose unintended consequences make the original problem worse

key: The Agreement/Uncertainty Matrix (Stacey): two axes, how certain a group is about what's going on and how far it agrees about what to do, separating simple, complicated and complex situations.
key_elements: two axes: certainty about what's going on and agreement about what to do (Stacey)
used to sort situations into simple, complicated and complex
